Method of Attack: Leverages SHA1 collision attack to create torrent files with identical SHA1 hashes but different executable content, allowing attackers to switch a benign EXE file with a malicious one without breaking torrent integrity. The malicious EXE decrypts and executes embedded shellcode to perform actions such as installing malware, backdoors, or banking trojans.
Uses SHA1 collision attack technique demonstrated by embedding two colliding PDF files inside different versions of an EXE file aligned in the same torrent data chunk.
Impacted Systems: BitTorrent clients (official BitTorrent client, Transmission-Qt client)
Attack Vector: Malicious torrent files seeded on BitTorrent networks that appear valid due to SHA1 hash collision
Indicators of Compromise: Torrent files with identical SHA1 hashes but different executable content
Proof-of-concept torrent files published on Github
EXE files containing encrypted shellcode and decryption keys switched during seeding
